finding: Subfebrile intrapartum maternal temperature was associated with higher rates of primary cesarean deliveries, assisted vaginal deliveries, early neonatal sepsis, neonatal intensive care unit admissions, and neonatal asphyxia or seizures.
mod_finding: Compared to women with a maximal intrapartum temperature of ≤37°C, women with subfebrile intrapartum temperature (37.1-37.9°C) had higher rates of caesarean deliveries and assisted vaginal deliveries.
